pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to Club 1541 | The King's School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Club 1541
Club 1541 is the home of former students, parents and staff of The King's School, Gloucester.
Launched in September 2018 as part of Headmaster David Morton’s plan to reconnect with our Alumni. All former students join on leaving the school, receiving full membership to Club 1541 which includes their tie or pin and invitations to Alumni exclusive events.
As well as wanting to keep in touch with our former students, we are also keen to stay close with the their parents as well as ex-staff members of King's. As such, when they leave the King's Community they are warmly welcomed into Club 1541, receiving honorary memberships.
Visit the Club 1541 website by clicking here.
New Digital Archive
We are delighted to officially launch our new digital archive and thanks to a generous donation from a former King's student, we haves already been able to digitalise school magazines from six different decades and share them with you.
Read the full story by clicking here.
Social Media
Social media is one of the quickest and easiest ways for you to stay in touch with the School, catch up with former friends and staff and keep up to date with events that are specifically for Alumni.
You can connect in a number of ways.
Follow the Club 1541 Facebook Page
Follow us on Instagram
Connect on the LinkedIn Group
Contact Us
For any queries about The Foundation or Alumni please contact the us using one of the following means.
George Smith The King's School Gloucester GL1 2BG
Tel: +44 (0)1452 337337 Email: [email protected]

pageCache.pageTitle: Strategic Development Plan | The King's School
pageCache.text:
Strategic Development Plan
King's has a long and inspiring history and we intend to ensure that the school thrives in the years ahead. To achieve this, every five years we publish a Strategic Development Plan to define and shape the school's development; this is the second Plan published by the current Headmaster.
The key theme for our 2023 - 2028 Strategic Development Plan is simply ‘Foundations’. Dating back to at least 1541 and following significant recent investment in facilities, the school clearly has a proud history but also enjoys current success. The main aim for the next five years therefore, is to build even stronger foundations which will help the school to thrive for centuries to come.
2023-2028 Strategic Development Plan:
We expect that there will be much to challenge us in the next five years, however, with clearly defined Ethos and Aims, allied to ambitious objectives, we are confident that King's will continue to develop and thrive - despite these challenges.
Our Ethos was defined in the 2018 Strategic Development Plan and continues in the current plan.

pageCache.text:
Welcome
King’s is one of the seven famous Cathedral Schools established by Henry VIII in 1541. Today we are a thriving, forward-thinking, independent day school with over 700 pupils. We welcome boys and girls, aged 3 to 18, offering academic excellence and a celebrated range of co-curricular activities, underpinned by outstanding pastoral care.
With small class sizes and inspiring teachers, King's offers a vibrant culture of energy and endeavour in a stunning historic setting adjacent to Gloucester Cathedral, which is where our daily school chapel is held. As a result, our school has a special sense of identity which encourages strong moral values and a powerful feeling of community.
King's aims to inspire all pupils to discover their own talents and reach their greatest possible achievement by participating in the wide range of cultural, intellectual, sporting, creative and performing arts activities available.
The unique features of King’s, which visitors identify time and again, are the inclusive community, the warmth of welcome and the level of individual care for our pupils.
Our Headmaster, Mr David Morton, is Chair of the Choir Schools’ Association. He is also a Lay Canon at Gloucester Cathedral.
We hope our website gives you a feel for the very special education on offer at King's. We would be delighted to welcome you to our school for a visit. For more information please contact our Admissions Office on 01452 337337 or email [email protected].

pageCache.pageTitle: Junior King's Values | The King's School
pageCache.text:
Junior King's Values
Values
Our King's SMART values underpin all that we do. Who needs rules when we are all aiming to be King's SMART?
Be friendly and considerate
Be helpful or supportive
Walk, do not run, when inside
Arrive on time
Be ready and properly equipped
Be co-operative
Take care with our work and appearance
Strive to do our best
Overcoming adversity both academically and socially
Embracing challenges
Persisting in the face of setbacks
Working together with others
Our education is based on our wider school values which are Respect, Responsibility, Kindness, Honesty, Equality, Individuality and Resilience.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to Little King's | The King's School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Little King's
Here at Little King's we start the journey for your little ones from the age of three to five. These first years are very important in building the foundations for your child's future. Our caring and experienced staff, in our separate and secluded setting, will make sure that your child has the very best start possible.
Children come to school with a wealth of learning, which has been acquired during the first three years at home. We aim to build on these foundations, through the provision of a curriculum which is stimulating, structured and balanced; which engages the child physically, intellectually, socially and emotionally; and which develops the child’s skills, concepts and attitudes.
As a result of our very individual curriculum we produce happy, confident and resilient children who are independent, ready and eager to learn because they have had the very best start.
The Good Schools Guide concluded...
"Learning is so fun that they barely realise they’re learning at all. Yet they leave at 11, more than ready for the senior school. ‘Warm, family-oriented and all-through, what’s not to like?’ said one parent. Links with the cathedral clinches the deal for many."
You can read their full review HERE.
If you would like more information, arrange a personal tour, or bring your child in for a Taster Session, please complete the enquiry form HERE and we will contact you.
We look forward to getting to know you.
Bethany Pedrick Head of Little King's
We encourage children to learn through discovery, creating structured experiences and fun activities that tap in to their natural fascination...
Meet our staff...
Being King's SMART
Here in Little King's, as well as the Junior School, we strive to be King's SMART at all times.
Be friendly and considerate
Be helpful or supportive
Walk, do not run, when inside
Arrive on time
Be ready and properly equipped
Be co-operative

Welcome to King's Junior School
Communicating the essence of a school is never easy and this is particularly true of King’s, which has so much to offer children beginning their exciting journey in education. However, I would like to highlight just a few qualities that I think make King’s truly outstanding.
As Gloucester’s Cathedral School, founded in 1541 by Henry VIII, we are hugely proud of our heritage and traditions. Every day we are inspired by one of the most beautiful medieval cathedrals in England; holding our morning assemblies in the Chapter House and our services in its Nave.
Our history and surroundings are wonderful, but King’s provides something even more valuable – a love of learning. We do this by presenting stimulating and engaging lessons and by encouraging children to pursue their personal interests. The range of co-curricular activities we provide is astonishingly varied and genuinely enriching.
While we celebrate individual talent and excellence, pupils of all ages have a very strong sense of community and soon become supportive team members. This blend of personal achievement and team spirit is one of the defining qualities of King’s.
As a Talking School, we place communication at the heart of everything we do. We believe that language is the foundation for learning, wellbeing, and relationships. Our ethos encourages children to express themselves confidently, listen actively, and engage thoughtfully with others. Through structured dialogue, restorative practices, and a culture of curiosity, we help pupils develop the skills to think critically, resolve differences, and build meaningful connections. Talking is not just an activity here—it is a way of learning and living together.
Growing-up can be challenging. Consequently, we ensure that the quality of our pastoral care matches the high quality of our teaching. We work in close partnership with parents to create a secure environment where children of all abilities can thrive and be happy.
You can read much more about us on this site, but if you are new to King’s, there is nothing better than seeing our School in action. I hope, therefore, that one day soon I will have the pleasure of welcoming you and your child to King’s for a visit. I would love to show you around our ‘remarkable’ school.
For more information please go to our visit us page where you can book an Open Event or Stay and Play session and find out general admissions information. Alternatively you can contact our friendly Admissions Team on 01452 337337 or email [email protected].
Anne Haas Head of King’s Junior School

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to the Senior School | The King's School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to the Senior School
On arrival at The King’s School, visitors always comment on our stunning campus of historic buildings and tranquil gardens, against the backdrop of glorious Gloucester Cathedral.
Alongside our modern, state-of-the-art Sports Hall and Performing Arts building, the campus is indeed a spectacular, inspirational place to work each day and home to a school which offers much more than initially meets the eye.
We have been proudly independent since 1541. Unlike many schools, we do not believe that ‘one size fits all’. This freedom allows us to choose the small class sizes, academic curriculum and assessment methods that we believe are best suited to our pupils.
King’s is small enough for us to know each child and to value them as an individual yet large enough to offer a very wide range of academic subjects and a spectacular array of co-curricular opportunities. Our subject teachers are specialists in their field and are therefore skilled at helping every pupil to fulfil their academic potential. Our value-added results each year are exceptional and our pupils develop the confidence, resilience and skills to stand them in good stead for the future.
Our family-friendly ethos creates a warm, welcoming community with strong links between parents, pupils and staff. This sense of community extends long after pupils leave school and results in a tangible sense of pride in having been a King’s pupil. We prepare our pupils not only to do their best individually, but also to reflect on their place in the wider world. Like so many of their predecessors, we want to ensure that today’s pupils are equipped to play a positive part in that wider community.
Truly, this is a school which can claim to demonstrate ‘history in the making’.
I hope that you will visit our wonderful school in the near future to discover these unique qualities which make King’s such an inspiring place to live and work each day.
David Morton Headmaster
"Pupils are attentive, well behaved and engage with their learning enthusiastically, developing skills, knowledge and independent thinking."
ISI Report October 2025
The highlights from our Foundation Day will give you an insight into the wonderful community that is King's.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to King's Sixth Form | The King's School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to King's Sixth Form
"Teaching in the sixth form encourages collaboration through practical work and projects, and challenge through online courses and entry into national competitions."
ISI Report October 2025
Our Sixth Form has between 120 and 130 pupils which allows us to be responsive in meeting students’ individual needs. With a typical Sixth Form class being between six and ten pupils, each pupil’s progress and well-being can be carefully monitored.
Our approach to teaching and learning emphasises collaboration, support and challenge in equal measure. We support, extend and challenge all pupils, and ensure that students with additional learning needs are supported. We take academic achievement seriously, but we also regard a holistic education of the whole person to be vitally important, and we equip our students with the values, attitudes, skills and knowledge that bring success in future employment, study and life. We do this by promoting independence, responsibility, initiative, awareness of self, and concern for others. Attending a Sixth Form within a school gives our students the best of both worlds. King’s Sixth Form students enjoy independence and freedom; however, they can still benefit from being part of a whole school community.
We offer a broad enrichment programme to our students in the Sixth Form. Individual careers advice and a selection of talks and visits support the process of application to higher and further education, and employment. We encourage initiative and provide an environment in which creativity can flourish and individual talent is recognised and nurtured. All this creates a solid foundation for our students to move out with confidence into the world beyond King’s.
We look forward to welcoming you and showing you life in King's Sixth Form.
To book a tour, or for any further information, please email [email protected] or visit our Admissions page: /admissions/admissions-process
Dr Tom Horler-Underwood Head of Sixth Form
The following article appeared in Current Archaeology. It is written by Chiz Harwood, who was the Archaeologist on the Dulverton Sixth Form Centre redevelopment, and gives a fascinating insight in to the project.

King's Sixth Form Centre transformed
In January 2021 we opened the newly transformed Sixth Form Centre in which we have preserved the beautiful period features of this historic building whilst creating bigger, brighter and more modern work and social spaces fit for 21st Century learning. pageCache.pageTitle: Set the stage for GCSE Shakespeare | The King's School
pageCache.text:
Set the stage for GCSE Shakespeare
Want to get GCSE-ready? Mystified by Macbeth? More familiar with Gnomeo & Juliet than Romeo and Juliet? This workshop is for you!
Join us for an interactive workshop which will introduce the play’s language, characters and themes via practical drama-based activities. You will leave the session with a stronger understanding of the play’s key themes and ideas and some practical techniques to help you approach your GCSE Shakespeare studies and exams with confidence.
The course will be run by Mrs Cassie Martin, an experienced examiner and teacher of English and Drama at GCSE and A Level. She holds an MA in Shakespeare and Education with Distinction from The Shakespeare Institute in Stratford-upon-Avon, part of the University of Birmingham.
Who should attend?
This course is for pupils aged 14 - 15, and in school years 9 & 10
When?
Wednesday 19th August
10am - 12pm: Macbeth - FULL
1pm - 3pm: Romeo and Juliet
How much is the course?

pageCache.pageTitle: Easter GCSE Revision Course | The King's School
pageCache.text:
Easter GCSE Revision Course
30th March - 2nd April 2026
Unlock your potential with our 4-day Easter GCSE Revision Courses at The King's School, Gloucester
Are you a student preparing for your GCSEs and looking to boost your confidence before the exams?
Or perhaps you struggle to stay motivated while revising at home alone?
The King's School has the perfect solution for you with our focused and supportive Easter GCSE Revision Course.
Taking place over the Easter break on Monday 30th March to Thursday 2nd April 2026, this course offers an invaluable opportunity for Year 11 students to strengthen their understanding and exam readiness. Whether you're a King's pupil or joining us from another school, you'll find a welcoming and academically rigorous environment designed to help you succeed.
Tailored Learning in Small Classes
At King's, we understand the importance of personalized attention, especially when preparing for such significant exams. That's why our Easter Revision Course features small class sizes, ensuring that every pupil receives the individual guidance they need. Our team of experienced teachers and examiners are experts in their fields, dedicated to helping you grasp challenging concepts and develop effective exam techniques.
Core Subject Coverage
Over three days you will cover Maths, English Language, English Literature and AQA Biology, Chemistry and Physics. On the fourth day, a selection of other subjects are available such as History, Business, Computer Science and Geography.
'I learned lots of techniques to approach each of the questions in the exam and the advice and feedback was helpful and made me feel more confident'
Daily Schedule
'Speaking as the parent of a child who finds it difficult to get started with independent study, this course has been a huge asset.'
Who should attend?
This course is ideal for students who need a confidence boost, whether due to anxiety about exams or simply because they find revising at home challenging. Our supportive environment will help you feel more in control and ready to tackle your GCSEs with renewed determination.
Don't miss this opportunity to take control of your revision and maximise your potential.
Course Costs and How to Book
Bookings are now closed but there are a few spaces for some subjects. Please email [email protected] for more information.

pageCache.pageTitle: The History of King's before 1950 | The King's School
pageCache.text:
The History of King's before 1950
Welcome to the fascinating history of King’s! Our school has a distinguished past that stretches back beyond King Henry VIII into the Middle Ages. Historical researchers will find many items of interest in this section of the website, which tells our story up to and including the Second World War. The school originated as part of the medieval Abbey of St Peter’s, it was re-founded by Henry VIII in 1541 and has links with the 17th century Archbishop Laud. The school then emerged as one of the country’s leading educational establishments under its 18th century headmasters, Maurice Wheeler and Thomas Stock.

pageCache.pageTitle: Historic Cathedral Schools launch the Three Choirs Schools Group | The King's School
pageCache.text:
Historic Cathedral Schools launch the Three Choirs Schools Group
We are delighted that King's as one of the country’s oldest cathedral schools has come together with Hereford Cathedral School and The King’s School, Worcester to form the Three Choirs Schools Group. This new partnership is designed to strengthen educational excellence, broaden opportunity and enhance collaboration across the three counties of Herefordshire, Gloucestershire and Worcestershire.
Rooted in a shared cathedral foundation and Christian ethos, the partnership brings together three schools with over two millennia of combined history, more than 2,600 pupils and a collective annual turnover of £50m. Each school is a charity committed to academic excellence, character formation and outstanding pastoral care, and the new group aims to amplify those strengths through structured collaboration.
The partnership has been created to enhance, rather than change, the identity of each school. All schools will retain their independence, legal status, governance and leadership. Rather than operating for profit or commercial purposes, the group is founded on shared values and a belief that collaboration can deliver richer opportunities for pupils, staff and the wider communities they serve.
You can find out more about the partnership and the benefits it will bring to families and communities by watching the short video below and by visiting our website.

pageCache.pageTitle: Early Birds Morning Club & Playmakers Aftercare | The King's School
pageCache.text:
Early Birds Morning Club & Playmakers Aftercare
Early Birds Morning Club and Playmakers Aftercare
Early Birds Morning Club for Preschool to Year 6: 7.45am to 8.15am
We have a new booking system for Early Birds Morning Club. It is now accessed through My School Portal in the clubs and activities section. This is available now for booking, and is run by Junior School Staff.
Playmakers Aftercare: 3.15pm to 5.30pm
We also have a new booking system for Playmakers Aftercare. It is now accessed through My School Portal in the clubs and activities section.
For both Early Birds Morning Club and Playmakers Aftercare, sessions need to be booked at the latest, the day before. If a session is needed as an emergency on the day please ring Junior School Reception (01452 337337).
If the date you require is not listed then unfortunately, the session is fully booked. Please note if you need to cancel a session, the session will still be charged, unless 24 hours notice has been given.
The booking system is live for Early Birds Morning Club and Playmakers Aftercare.
Any queries please e-mail [email protected]
King's After School Club
Led by our dedicated Lunchtime Supervisor, Morgan Padfield, the club provides a warm, supportive environment where children can relax and enjoy their time beyond the classroom.
The atmosphere is calm, welcoming, and centred on helping children feel at ease while they create, explore, and have fun after a busy school day.
Arts and crafts activities
Relaxed, homely activities to help children unwind
An enhanced snack provision for every pupil
Club Times & Pricing
3.30pm - 4pm: £4 per session*
3.30pm – 6pm (5.30pm for Little King's) : £11 per session*
How to book
Please book via My School Portal: Navigate to Sports and Co-curricular → Activities → After Care.
Parents will be billed at the end of term.
*Late charges will apply
Contact Details:
For any queries, please e-mail: [email protected] , or phone: 07919 753376
Atlas Camps Holiday Club for Years 1 to 6
Holiday Club, provided by Atlas Camps, runs throughout School holidays including the Half-Term holidays, starting at £35 per day, discounts are available for full week bookings and siblings.
To book a place please visit Atlas Camps. For any queries please phone Atlas Camps on: 0800 7720743, or email: [email protected].
